leftEvidence.role: Israel in apostolic argument and final vision
leftEvidence.title: Former outsiders are brought near to Israel’s commonwealth

points.label: Israel setting and claim
points.left: Gentile readers are told they were once excluded from Messiah, alienated from Israel’s commonwealth, and strangers to covenants.
points.right: Paul lists circumcision, Israelite ancestry, Benjamin, Hebrew identity, law, zeal, and blamelessness as grounds for confidence in flesh.

points.label: Response and consequence
points.left: through Christ those far away are brought near, hostility is broken, and one new humanity and one household are described.
points.right: he then counts those gains as loss because of knowing Christ and pursuing resurrection.

payload.posture: Ephesians addresses people once outside Israel’s commonwealth, while Philippians presents Paul’s Israelite credentials as real gains he refuses to use as grounds of confidence.

rightEvidence.role: Israel in apostolic argument and final vision
rightEvidence.title: Paul counts Israelite credentials as loss because of Christ

payload.tension: One passage names exclusion overcome through nearness; the other names inherited advantage surrendered for Christ.
payload.title: Alienation from Israel and confidence in Israelite ancestry
